title: Market Structures: Competition, Monopoly, and the Middle Ground

questions.question: A firm in perfect competition is a price taker because:
options: Each firm is too small relative to the market to influence price
questions.rationale: With very many sellers of a homogenous product, no single firm's output decision can move the market price, so each takes the price as given.

questions.question: Which feature distinguishes monopolistic competition from perfect competition?
questions.rationale: Monopolistic competition keeps many sellers and free entry but differentiates products by brand, quality, or location — giving each firm limited pricing power.

questions.question: A natural monopoly arises when:
options: The government grants an exclusive licence
A firm owns all skilled workers
Economies of scale are so large that one firm serves the market at lowest cost
questions.rationale: When average cost keeps falling over the entire demand range, one firm can supply the whole market more cheaply than several — Indian Railways' network is the lesson's example.

questions.question: The kinked demand curve is associated with which market structure?
questions.rationale: In oligopoly, rivals match price cuts but ignore price rises, producing a kink in the demand curve and sticky prices.

questions.question: Strategic interdependence — each firm considering rivals' reactions — is the defining trait of:
questions.rationale: Because oligopoly has few large firms, each one's pricing and output decisions materially affect the others, forcing strategic behaviour.

questions.question: A cartel is best described as:
options: An explicit collusive agreement among rival firms
questions.rationale: Cartels are collusive oligopoly agreements — illegal in India under the Competition Act, 2002.

questions.question: Which Indian industry most closely approximates perfect competition?
questions.rationale: Small farmers selling homogenous produce in vegetable mandis face many buyers and sellers with no individual price control — closest real-world approximation.

questions.question: Compared with perfect competition, a monopolist typically:
options: Produces more at a lower price
Produces less and charges a higher price
questions.rationale: A monopoly restricts output below the competitive level and prices above it, creating deadweight loss — the basis for anti-trust and regulation.

questions.question: In monopolistic competition, long-run economic profits are competed away mainly because of:
questions.rationale: Easy entry means profits attract new differentiated sellers until excess profit is normalised, even though brands persist.

questions.question: A market with a few large sellers of a homogenous product like cement is best classified as:
questions.rationale: Cement, steel, and aluminium are the lesson's examples of oligopoly with homogenous products and high entry barriers.
